title: Forge release-build-plan v1
description:
Standalone `forge.release-build-plan/v1` candidate request.

Deserialization is a tolerant same-major compatibility reader, not current acceptance. The
strict release gate must separately enforce exact schema identity, current enum branches,
semantic invariants, and canonical bytes before this request can influence an Authority
execution.

GitObjectIdV2Data.description: A validated object ID paired with its Git object format.

GitSha1ObjectIdV2Data.description: A validated full SHA-1 Git object ID.

GitSha256ObjectIdV2Data.description: A validated full SHA-256 Git object ID.

ReleaseBuildBinaryData.description: The fixed binary requested by a release build plan.

ReleaseBuildDependencyResolutionData.description: The fixed dependency-resolution mode requested by a release build plan.

ReleaseBuildNetworkData.description: The fixed network mode requested by a release build plan.

ReleaseBuildPackageNameData.description: One bounded Cargo package name used by the release protocol.

ReleaseBuildPackageVersionData.description: One bounded Cargo package version used by the release protocol.

ReleaseBuildPlanOutputsData.description: Target-derived, reviewable output basenames requested by a release build plan.

ReleaseBuildPlanPackageData.description: The fixed package requested by a release build plan.

ReleaseBuildPlanPurposeData.description:
Why a candidate emits a release build plan.

The plan is an untrusted semantic request to an external authority. It is never an executable
command, builder record, qualification result, approval, or release evidence.

ReleaseBuildProfileData.description: The fixed Cargo profile requested by a release build plan.

ReleaseBuildTargetData.description:
One target accepted by the release plan/apply protocol.

This is intentionally separate from the diagnostic observation contract so additions cannot
silently change the already published observation-v1 schema.
